title: Two ships hit by drones of unknown origin off Bulgarian coast – Europe live
summary:
Rescue operations underway after one vessel is sunk in the Black Sea and another damaged

blocks.text: 11 crew members from sunken vessel hit by drone still missing near Bulgarian coast
The latest update from Bulgaria says that 11 crew members from the sunken ship are still missing.
The number of people rescued from the ship has now gone up to five, with authorities hoping they will be able to offer more insight into what happened overnight.

blocks.text: The ministers get asked about Trump’s diesel deal with Putin.
They don’t really offer any hot takes on this.
Germany’s Wadephul says that Europe needs to keep talking to Trump, and keep imposing sanctions on Russia.
Poland’s Sikorski makes a domestic point, putting pressure on Poland’s Maga-friendly president Karol Nawrocki to intervene with Trump directly.
Norway’s Espen Barth Eide also focuses on Europe’s resolve, more than anything else.
By the way, you can watch the Warsaw Security Forum panel with Barth Eide, Miliband, Sikorski, and Wadephul here.
'We are facing a really testing period' on Ukraine, Russian hybrid warfare, UK's Miliband says
UK’s Miliband is next.

He draws on his family’s history, saying his mother found refuge in Warsaw during the second world war, and he had “an amazing visit” to the Jewish Historical Institute this morning where he saw documents about his family’s history.
“It is a reminder of what war means for the ravaging of people’s lives and the uprooting of people’s lives.”
But he then moves on to Ukraine as he says:

“I think our job is not to be analysts, but to lead. We are four and a half years into this warm and the truth is that our resolve is being tested. Our resolve is being tested as far as Ukraine is concerned, resolve is being tested with Russian hybrid warfare, and our job is to stop and to respond. I feel a sense of confidence, but I don’t think we can be complacent at all. We are facing a really testing period. Putin is not winning this war, but him not winning is not good enough for us yet. And therefore what we do in the coming months, whether it is on sanctions, continuing to increase the pressure on Russia, whether it is the fiscal support for Ukraine, whether it’s defensive support for Ukraine, all of this really, really matters, and it matters morally, and it matters also to European security.”
Support for Ukraine over the coming winter is critical, EU ministers say
The four ministers are speaking now.
Poland’s Sikorski says he “regrets” that Europe “wasted” the first two years of the Russian invasion of Ukraine, and is only now “catching up” when it comes to rearmaments.

“By the end of the decade, we will have a combined army, even just around the Baltic and the Eastern flank, that Putin would be crazy to attack. But if that is our calendar, that would be too late for Ukraine,” he says.
He says it’s critical to sustain Ukraine through the coming winter.
Germany’s Wadephul says Europe is “more united than we were at the beginning of the war,” and “have more capabilities.”
“The winter will be challenging, but we know what to do.”
Over in Warsaw, Poland’s parliament speaker Włodzimierz Czarzasty is beginning his opening speech telling the audience that Europe is “at the turning point” of “civilisational” significance.
Addressing the Warsaw Security Forum, he says “for those who have any doubts that the president of the Russian Federation is a murderer and aggressor, and Ukraine is a victim.”
He says “it has to be said: there is no free Poland and free Europe, without a free Ukraine.”

Just as he says it, Poland issues a (now fairly routine) emergency alert to residents of a south-eastern region neighbouring Ukraine, putting them on high alert because of Russian strikes across the border.
The foreign ministers of Britain, Germany, Poland and Norway should be up on the main stage shortly.
Morning opening: Two ships hit by drones off Bulgarian coast
Jakub Krupa
Drones of unknown origin struck two ships in the Black Sea off Bulgaria this morning, sinking one and prompting emergency rescue operations, the country’s prime minister Rumen Radev said.

blocks.caption: Bulgarian prime minister Rumen Radev addresses the media following an incident in Bulgaria's Black Sea economic zone last week. Photograph: Spasiyana Sergieva/Reuters

blocks.text: Only one person was rescued from the sunken vessel, and 15 people were picked up from the other one.
The attack comes exactly a week after a similar incident in which one ship sank with its crew on board, and the other one was evacuated, with 18 people rescued.
PM Radev said the attacks were “absolutely unacceptable,” and said he would seek assistance from Nato and the European Union.
He said that while there is no “clear and conclusive evidence to attribute responsibility” yet, “the logic suggests that the outcome benefits the Russian Federation.”
The European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, said “the Black Sea has become another front of escalation of the Russian war in Ukraine.”

“This is unacceptable. I strongly condemn the drone attacks on merchant ships near Bulgaria’s coast. Putting the lives of the crew in grave danger and threatening security in the Black Sea. We stand with Bulgaria and thank its rescuers for their swift response. Those responsible should be held accountable.”

The incident comes amid growing fears about Russia’s war against Ukraine and as several European foreign ministers meet at the Warsaw Security Forum in Poland, including Britain’s Ed Miliband, Germany’s Johann Wadephul, and Ukraine’s Andrii Sybiha.
I will monitor their comments and bring you the top lines.
Separately, the French high school protests are expected to intensify today after key groups called for “a day of mobilisation” across the country.
Over in Spain, the Spanish royals are expected to visit the autonomous city of Ceuta in northern Africa, which continues to see its every day’s life disrupted by the migration crisis.

In Sweden, the Social Democrats leader Magdalena Andersson is due to report back on the progress of her talks on government formation today. But early reports suggest she does not quite have everything lined up yet, and the process is likely to take more time.

Finally, in the Vatican, Pope Leo is expected to be hospitalised today to remove a lung nodule discovered in his body to test it if the lesion is malignant. He is likely to stay there for about a week.
So, lots for us to cover. I will bring you all the key lines here.
It’s Monday, 13 October 2026, it’s Jakub Krupa here, and this is Europe Live.
Good morning.
